title: Your Mission: Locate the Evidence
body:
You have learned how land and shorelines can change. Now investigate a different question: how do we know people lived in the islands long ago? Your mission is to build a careful museum explanation using a place, a find and what that find supports.

Archaeology studies past life through objects, remains and the places where they are found. Context means the recorded setting: location, layer and relationship to other finds. A find separated from its context can lose useful information.

Start with the locator. Tabon is at Lipuun Point in Quezon, Palawan. Callao Cave is in Peñablanca, Cagayan, in northern Luzon. These dots locate two sites, not every place with evidence of early people. They do not show an ancient travel route between the caves.
clues: Locate Tabon
The Tabon dot lies on Palawan, southwest of the Callao dot. A modern locator tells us where the site is, not who travelled there.
Locate Callao
Callao is in Cagayan on Luzon, not on Palawan. Two different locations can preserve different kinds of evidence.
Record the setting
A find record connects a sample with its location and layer. Moving it before recording that information can remove part of the evidence.
task: A find is photographed but its location and layer are not recorded. What important information is missing?
Its archaeological context
Its brightest display colour
The length of its modern place name
Proof that every island had the same people
reason: Context connects a find with its recorded place and surroundings. A photograph alone does not replace that information.

glossary.definition: The recorded place, layer and relationships of a find.

title: Watch How: Make a Tabon Evidence Card
body:
Tabon Cave in Palawan has yielded human remains, including evidence of Homo sapiens, and many stone tools. Homo sapiens is the scientific name of our species. A stone tool is an object shaped or used by people; it is not itself a human bone.

Worked example: turn a source description into an evidence card. Step 1. Name the place: Tabon, Palawan. Step 2. Name the find: human remains identified as Homo sapiens. Step 3. State a supported conclusion: people of our species were present there long ago.

Now add a limit. This find does not identify every ancestor of every Filipino. Different finds can come from different times, so do not give every Tabon object the same age. The illustration is a summary card, not a photograph of an original find.
clues: Read the place
The Tabon card names Palawan. Keep that label with the evidence rather than exchanging it with the Callao label.
Read the find type
Human remains and stone tools are different evidence types. Tools can help investigate activities; remains help investigate people and their physical features.
Check the claim
The Homo sapiens identification supports presence of our species at the site. It does not produce a complete family tree for living Filipinos.
task: Which museum statement is supported by the Tabon evidence card?
Homo sapiens were present at Tabon long ago
Every Filipino descended from one person at Tabon
All tools at Tabon have exactly one age
Tabon and Callao are the same cave
reason: The card connects a named site with Homo sapiens remains. That supports presence at the site, not a claim about every family or every find.

glossary.definition: An object shaped or used by people to do a task.

title: Try Together: Compare Callao and Tabon
body:
Callao Cave in Cagayan has yielded ancient teeth and bones studied by a research team. The researchers described Homo luzonensis as a distinct ancient human species in 2019. It is not simply another name for Homo sapiens. A fossil is a preserved remain or trace of past life. A species is a scientific grouping studied through features and relationships. Scientists compare features and other evidence when making such identifications.

Compare the cards together. Both refer to human evidence from caves. Their locations and species identifications differ. Tabon is on Palawan; Callao is on Luzon.

A 2019 University of the Philippines report described the Callao fossils as about 50,000 to 67,000 years old. That is an age report about studied material, not the year scientists found it and not proof of the first arrival of people anywhere in the islands. New work may refine explanations. No appearance or full life story is reconstructed in these teaching cards.
clues: Compare like with like
Both cards name a place and an evidence type. Compare those categories before making a conclusion.
Keep names distinct
The labels Homo sapiens and Homo luzonensis identify different species. Neither name is a ranking of living communities.
Separate age and research
The research description appeared in 2019. The material studied is much older; a publication date is not the lifetime of the ancient people.
task: Which comparison uses both evidence cards correctly?
Both contain human evidence, but the sites and species labels differ
Both labels name the same species at the same site
A 2019 publication means the ancient people lived in 2019
The cards prove one cave contains all Philippine ancestors
reason: Compare place, evidence and identification separately. Tabon and Callao preserve different records, and a modern research date is not an ancient lifetime.

glossary.definition: A preserved remain or trace of past life.
A scientific grouping studied through features and relationships.

title: Your Turn: Read Time Carefully
body:
Time information answers different questions. A research timeline tells us when modern study happened: National Museum investigations at Tabon included 1962 to 1965; the Homo luzonensis description was published in 2019. These dates do not mean the ancient people lived then.

An age estimate describes how old a find may be. A range gives limits rather than one exact year. With years ago, a larger number means farther into the past.

Try the clearly fictional range exercise. Find A is estimated at 1,000 to 2,000 years ago. Find B is estimated at 1,500 to 2,500 years ago. The ranges overlap from 1,500 to 2,000. You cannot be certain which find is older using these ranges alone. These are made-up numbers for practice, not dates for Tabon or Callao. The oldest evidence found so far is not necessarily the first person who arrived.
clues: Research dates
1962 to 1965 and 2019 describe modern research milestones in this lesson, not ancient lifetimes.
Find the overlap
The fictional ranges both include the interval from 1,500 to 2,000 years ago. Overlap leaves more than one possible order.
Check what is dated
An age belongs to the material studied using a particular method. A nearby object does not automatically share exactly that age.
task: Fictional finds A and B have overlapping age ranges. What is the careful conclusion?
Their exact older-younger order is not certain from these ranges alone
Find B must be older in every possible case
Find A must be older in every possible case
Both must have been made in 2019
reason: The fictional ranges overlap. Both orders are possible within them, so the ranges alone cannot establish a certain older-younger order.

glossary.definition: An interval between possible ages, rather than one exact age.
When a modern investigation or publication happened.

title: Make a Choice: Protect the Record
body:
A visitor notices a possible old object at a managed site. It is tempting to pick it up, clean it or take it as a souvenir. Those actions can damage the object or remove information about its setting. Leave it in place and tell the responsible site staff. Students should not excavate or test finds themselves.

Human remains are preserved parts of people who lived in the past. They are not game prizes, props or objects to handle for entertainment. Care involves responsible specialists and respect for communities connected with heritage.

You may save an authored explanation in your Evidence Journal. That bookmark is a learning reference, not ownership of an original object. A photo, copy or teaching card should be labelled honestly. Pictures of models do not become original archaeological evidence.
clues: Protect the place
Keeping a find where it was noticed preserves the chance for responsible staff to record its setting.
Protect people and heritage
Respectful care considers the people represented and the communities involved, not just the appearance of a display.
Label the learning copy
A journal bookmark or classroom card records learning. It is not an original fossil, an excavation permit or a cultural object owned by the player.
task: A visitor sees a possible old object at a managed heritage site. What action protects the evidence?
Leave it in place and notify site staff
Wash it before telling staff
Move it to make a more attractive photograph
Take it home and remember its approximate location
reason: Leaving the object in place and informing responsible staff protects its context and avoids untrained handling. A learning token never gives ownership of real remains.

glossary.definition: A copy of an object, not the original.

title: Field Journal: Build Your Museum Explanation
body:
Your museum explanation should connect evidence with a claim, not just collect impressive names. Use this structure: at this place, researchers studied this find; it supports this conclusion; it does not tell us everything.

Connect the mission ideas. The locator distinguishes Tabon in Palawan from Callao in Cagayan. Evidence cards distinguish find types and species identifications. Research dates differ from ancient ages. Estimated ranges can leave uncertainty. Context and respectful care preserve opportunities to learn.

Try one final comparison. A report says Homo sapiens remains were studied at Tabon and teeth and bones identified as Homo luzonensis were studied at Callao. You can explain the different records without claiming an exact travel route, one ancestor for everyone, or a complete life story. Save useful opened clues in your journal if you want to revisit them.
clues: Connect the categories
Use the place, find type and supported conclusion together. A site name alone does not explain the evidence.
Keep time questions separate
When something was studied and how old it is are different questions. A modern discovery does not make the find modern.
Prepare the next question
These sites show parts of a complex human past. The next mission examines population movements using more than one kind of source.
task: Which report connects evidence with a careful conclusion?
Tabon and Callao provide different records of ancient human presence, with limits to what each can show
The two caves prove every family has one exact origin
A publication date gives the first arrival date of all people
Any drawing of a cave is an original fossil record
reason: The report connects the named sites with human evidence while recognizing limits. More sources are needed for claims about routes, ancestry or first arrivals.

glossary.definition: Information used to support or question a claim.
